concept_title: 보랏빛 달밤의 매화 무대, 뱀과 렌
revision_note: V1 (2ac3ad0) rejected by the owner: too many borders. V2 (73a2823) merged the sky, both lattice doors and the moon/cloud layer into one back plate, shrank the clear rim 2.5 -> 1.0 mm and rendered clear acrylic see-through in the assembly preview. V3 (657a484) recomposed the scene but the owner prefers V2 ("v2가 낫다고 한거야"), so V4 starts from the V2 design: the V2 composition is restored unchanged (sky 90 mm, doors 85 mm, moon/clouds 60 mm, tree plate 72 mm at x=112, serpent 55 mm at x=115, character 84 mm at x=170 on row 12) as the base; the owner's two V4 requests are applied on top in the next step.
clear_border_rationale: docs/laser-cut-quality.md fixes no rim minimum; its hard limits are the 0.035 mm curve deviation and the 12 mm load-path floor on the buffered silhouette. 1.0 mm is the smallest round offset that still keeps UV ink 0.5 mm inside the cut edge under a 0.5 mm print registration error. Exception: the blossom tree keeps 1.2 mm because a 1.0 mm contour over its ~300-blossom canopy cannot be fitted within the laser_paths segment gate (1.5 segments per mm) at any workable simplification; 1.2 mm is the smallest rim that passes.

overlays.note: left lattice door butted against the sky's left edge, bottoms aligned
right lattice door butted against the sky's right edge, bottoms aligned
moon and both cloud islands (including V1's unused 34 x 6.9 mm upper-right cloud) registered over the sky; the disc lands ~10 mm right of the sky centre as in the concept

front_view_policy.note: ORIGIN is a deliberately stacked centre scene (tree across the moon, serpent behind the character): polygon occlusion is by design and overstates visual blocking. Numbers are recorded per piece in validation_report.json; composition acceptance is the vision-checked assembly preview against the supplied concept art. Structural checks (row clearance, overhang, load path, gaps) stay hard.
